stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190M for co-orbital security
stories.body: True Anomaly secured $190 million in a Series C funding round, bringing its valuation to $1.6 billion. The funding is aimed at enhancing co-orbital security and space domain awareness, showcasing the DoD's increasing reliance on commercial capabilities. With defense pull-through becoming a headline, True Anomaly is positioning itself as a key player in the national security landscape.
stories.soWhat: It's clear that the Pentagon's appetite for private sector innovation is growing, and True Anomaly's success could set a precedent for future funding in the sector.

stories.head: Icarus Robotics picks KULR for Space Station battery needs
stories.body: Icarus Robotics has tapped KULR Technology Group to provide batteries for its space robots, a move that underscores the importance of reliable power sources in space operations. The partnership could pave the way for more robust robotic operations on the International Space Station, where every watt counts. KULR's technology is expected to enhance the performance and longevity of these robots.
stories.soWhat: As space missions become more complex, the need for dependable energy solutions will only grow, making KULR's role crucial in the emerging robotics landscape.

stories.head: Florida startup SOAR tackles small debris with UT partnership
stories.body: Florida-based startup SOAR has partnered with the University of Texas to develop a passive system for trapping small space debris. This initiative highlights the growing concern over space junk, with investment in debris mitigation technologies becoming increasingly vital. The collaboration aims to attract further academic and commercial interest in debris management solutions.
stories.soWhat: If SOAR can prove its technology works, we might see a shift in how the industry approaches space debris—less about avoiding it and more about actively managing it.

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
